2027-07-13.title: Second Tuesday of Kaitha
2027-07-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: A friend of the world becomes an enemy of God
2027-07-13.alt: Season of Kaitha (Qaita, Summer), which follows the Season of the Apostles: the season of the Church's growth and harvest, when we remember the apostles, martyrs and saints who sowed the Gospel and watered it with their blood, and keep ourselves ready for the coming of the Lord. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari. The calendar's own headings: “A friend of the world becomes an enemy of God”; “Beatitudes”.
2027-07-13.verse: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
theo: On the second Tuesday of Kaitha the readings begin with a question that every family, parish and village has asked at some time: “Those conflicts and disputes among you, where do they come from?” James does not blame the weather, the neighbours or the committee. He points inward: “Do they not come from your cravings that are at war within you?” The word he uses for cravings is the one from which we get our word hedonism, the pull toward pleasure. The war outside begins with a war inside: “You want something and do not have it; so you commit murder. And you covet something and cannot obtain it; so you engage in disputes and conflicts.” James uses the strongest words on purpose, because envy, left to grow, walks the road of Cain. Even prayer can be infected by it: “You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, in order to spend what you get on your pleasures.” A prayer that only wants to add to our pile has not yet become a prayer.

Then the language grows sharper: “Adulterers! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God?” The prophets called Israel an unfaithful wife when she ran after other lovers, and James uses the same voice for a Church that wants Christ and also every prize the world hands out. “The world” here is not creation, which God made good and loved so much that he gave his Son (John 3:16). It is the order of life that organises itself without God and measures a person by what he owns and what others say of him. Against it James sets the jealous love of God: “God yearns jealously for the spirit that he has made to dwell in us.” God is not the rival of our happiness; he is a lover who wants us whole. And his answer to our cravings is a gift, not a rule: “But he gives all the more grace; therefore it says, ‘God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.’” Then comes the short road home: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.”

The Gospel shows what the grace given to the humble looks like. In Luke's Sermon on the Plain, Jesus “looked up at his disciples” and speaks four blessings and four woes. “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.” The verb is in the present: the kingdom is theirs now. “Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.” Jesus is not praising misery, and he is not saying that hunger is good. He is saying that God has taken the side of the one whose only possession is God, and that the reversal is certain. The fourth blessing is the one the martyrs of the Church lived: “Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you, revile you, and defame you on account of the Son of Man. Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for surely your reward is great in heaven.” The Church in Kaitha looks at her martyrs and sees this joy in a human face.

Then come the four woes: “But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation.” A woe is a lament, like the cry over a house about to fall, and not a curse. Jesus grieves for those whose comfort is already complete, who have nothing left to hope for. The last woe stings the preacher and the politician most: “Woe to you when all speak well of you, for that is what their ancestors did to the false prophets.” Put James and Luke side by side. The one who owns the kingdom does not need to go to war for a plot of land, a seat on a committee or a good name; the one who is ruled by cravings is never full. In Kerala, where a quarrel over a boundary or an inheritance can run for years in the courts and can even divide a family at the church door, the reading puts a gentle and hard question: what are we really fighting for, and did we first ask God for it in the right way?
outline: A war outside begins with a war inside: where do our quarrels come from?
Envy and the road of Cain; the prayer that only wants to add to our pile.
Point 2 · Friend of the world, friend of God
The jealous love of God; grace for the humble; submit and resist.
The kingdom is already theirs; the reversal Jesus promises; the consolation we must not settle for.
“Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.”
live: Before your next prayer for something you want, ask: would I still want it if no one ever knew I had it? Offer the wish to God and ask for what you truly need.
Think of one family or parish quarrel that has run too long. Make the first move this week: a call, a visit, a cup of tea.
fathers: Do you want to be great? Begin with the least. You are planning a great building that will rise to the sky? Think first of the foundation of humility. The higher the building, the deeper the foundation must be dug.

The bread in your cupboard belongs to the hungry; the coat hanging in your wardrobe belongs to the one who has none; the shoes you do not wear belong to the barefoot; the money in your vault belongs to the needy.
Not to let the poor share in our goods is to steal from them and to take away their life; what we hold is not our own, but theirs.
magis: The tenth commandment requires that envy be banished from the human heart. Envy is a capital sin: sadness at the sight of another's goods and the immoderate desire to get them for oneself.
The Lord grieves over the rich, because they find their consolation in the abundance of goods. The poor in spirit are those to whom the kingdom already belongs.
Giving to the poor is not an act of charity only; it is a payment of what is owed, a work of justice pleasing to God.
saints: Second Tuesday of Kaitha. In the Latin calendar, St Henry (an optional memorial).

13–18 July: the second week of Kaitha. Tue 13 and Wed 14: Second Tuesday and Wednesday of Kaitha. Thu 15: Sts Kuriakose and Julitta, an Ordinary Feast of the Oriental tradition (in the Latin calendar, St Bonaventure). Fri 16: the Second Friday of Kaitha, Mar Mari, disciple of Mar Addai, and Our Lady of Mount Carmel, an Important Marian Feast. Sat 17: Second Saturday of Kaitha. Sun 18: Third Sunday of Kaitha. Looking ahead: St Mary Magdalene on Thursday 22 July, and St Alphonsa, the first woman of India to be raised to the altars, on Wednesday 28 July.
2027-07-13.prayer: Lord God, you love us with a jealous love and give grace to the humble. Quiet the cravings that make war within us and in our homes. Teach us to ask for what is good, to share what we have, and to count ourselves blessed when we have you alone. Turn our quarrels into peace, our envy into thanksgiving, and our fear of what others say into joy in your kingdom. Through Jesus Christ our Lord, who with you and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the poor man's bread and the rich man's wine are placed on the same altar, and the same Lord gives himself to both. Whoever receives him cannot go on counting what the neighbour has: in the Body of Christ the hungry are filled, and the one who comes to the table with empty hands is already an heir of the kingdom.

quick: James: our fights come from cravings within; friendship with the world is enmity with God; God gives grace to the humble.
Luke: blessed are the poor, the hungry, the weeping and the hated for the Son of Man; woe to the rich, the full, the laughing and the praised.
Together: the one who owns the kingdom does not need to quarrel for scraps.
2027-07-13.action: Make the first move toward peace with one person with whom you have quarrelled, and pray for them by name.
2027-07-13.question: What am I fighting for, and have I asked God for it?

family.explain: Jesus looked at his friends and said: blessed are you who are poor, you who are hungry, you who cry. Why blessed? Because God is close to them and the kingdom of God is theirs. Jesus does not mean that being hungry is good. He means that God never forgets the one who has nothing, and that those who trust him will be filled. And he asks us to be like him and to share what we have, so that nobody in our village goes to bed hungry.
family.intention: We pray for families who are poor, for those who are quarrelling, and for the people who share their food with others.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there somebody in our street or parish whom we can help this week with food, a visit or a kind word?”

illus: In a village near Changanassery (a story told to illustrate the reading) two brothers had not spoken for eleven years because of a boundary stone between their rubber plots. The case dragged through the court, and each brother told his sons never to give way. One July night the river rose, and both families had to climb to the parish hall. The brothers found themselves on the same mat, wet and ashamed, with their old mother between them. In the morning the water had gone down, and the boundary stone was gone with it. The elder brother looked at the field and said quietly, ‘The water has done in one night what the court could not do in eleven years.’ The younger poured him a cup of tea. Nobody mentioned the stone again.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called the poor blessed and gave your Church the kingdom as an inheritance. Gather us now; heal what is at war in us and among us, and make us humble enough to receive your grace. Amen.
share: Those conflicts and disputes among you, where do they come from? (James 4:1). What is the real source of the quarrel I carry?
God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble (James 4:6). Where do I need to bend my pride this week?
Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God (Luke 6:20). What do I cling to that I should hold more lightly?
Woe to you when all speak well of you (Luke 6:26). Do I fear the opinion of people more than the judgment of God?
pm.resp: Lord, give us your grace and make us humble.
interc: For the families in our parish who are divided by quarrels over property or old wounds, that the Lord may bring them to peace.
For the poor, the hungry and those who weep, that they may be filled and comforted, and that we may not forget them.
For those who preach and lead, that they may not seek the praise of people more than the truth.
For Christians who are hated and reviled for the name of Jesus, that they may rejoice and stand firm.
For ourselves, that we may ask rightly, share gladly and submit to God.
pm.close: Father, you give grace to the humble and the kingdom to the poor. Keep us from the cravings that divide us, and lead us to the joy of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, James begins today with a question we all know: where do our quarrels come from? He answers like a good doctor. They come from cravings that make war inside us (James 4:1). We want something, we do not get it, and we turn on those nearest to us.

Think of the quarrels we have seen: over a boundary, a share of the land, a seat in a committee, a word that was never forgiven. James says that friendship with the world is enmity with God. By the world he means the way of living in which everything is measured by what I have and what people say of me.

But God is not a rival to our joy. He loves us with a jealous love, and he gives more grace to the humble (James 4:6). So James gives us the way back: submit to God, resist the devil, and the devil will flee.

Jesus shows us what that grace looks like. “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God” (Luke 6:20). Not will be: is. The one who has God has everything, and has no need to fight over scraps. And he warns us: “Woe to you when all speak well of you” (Luke 6:26). It is easy to live for applause.
This week let us make one peace. Let us ask God for what we truly need, share a little of what we have, and be glad that the kingdom belongs to the poor and the humble. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: blessed are the poor, for the kingdom of God is theirs. That means God loves people who have little, and he wants us to share with them. When you quarrel with your brother or sister, say sorry first. That is how people become friends of God!

intro: Theme: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.”
The war within that becomes war without, the grace that God gives to the humble, and the kingdom that already belongs to the poor.

points.h: Where do our quarrels come from?
sub: Envy and the road of Cain.
q: The Lord said to Cain, “Why are you angry, and why has your countenance fallen? If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin is lurking at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it.”
Those conflicts and disputes among you, where do they come from? Do they not come from your cravings that are at war within you?
points.apply: Name the craving behind one quarrel you carry, and hand it to God in prayer.

sub: Friend of the world, enemy of God.
Submit, resist, and the devil will flee.
q: Toward the scorners he is scornful, but to the humble he shows favor.
Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
points.apply: Bend your pride this week in one small matter: say sorry first.

sub: Hunger and tears will be reversed.
Woe to the comfortable and the praised.
q: But the meek shall inherit the land, and delight themselves in abundant prosperity.
“Woe to you when all speak well of you, for that is what their ancestors did to the false prophets.
points.apply: Share food, money or time with one person who has less than you.

concl: Our quarrels begin in our cravings; grace begins in humility and the kingdom begins with the poor.
Let us make peace first, and let us be glad to be citizens of a kingdom that cannot be bought.
2027-07-13.resolve: This week, make the first move toward peace with one person, ask God for what you truly need, and share with someone who has less.
